ai.literal: Even if thought of, unceasing great joy because of causing, even more than toddy, love is sweet.
ai.translation: Love is sweeter than wine, for it brings great and unceasing joy even when merely thought of.
ai.modern: நினைத்தாலே நீங்காத பெருமகிழ்ச்சியைத் தருவதால், காதலின் இன்பம் கள்ளை விட இனிமையானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the sweetness of love to that of intoxicating liquor. While liquor gives pleasure only when consumed, love brings great and unceasing joy ('தீராப் பெருமகிழ்') even when one merely thinks of the beloved ('உள்ளினும்'). Therefore, the speaker concludes that love is far sweeter than wine ('கள்ளினும் காமம் இனிது'). The contrast highlights the enduring and mental nature of romantic love compared to physical intoxication.

ai.literal: In whatever measure one thing sweet indeed see love, oneself lover when thinking that which comes one thing is not.
ai.translation: Behold, love is sweet in every possible way; for when one thinks of the lover, nothing sorrowful comes of it.
ai.modern: காதல் எல்லா வகையிலும் இனிமையானது; ஏனெனில், தாம் விரும்பும் காதலரை நினைக்கும்போது துன்பம் தருவது எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The speaker declares that love is entirely sweet in every possible measure. Unlike other worldly experiences where separation brings only pain, love is unique because merely thinking of the beloved brings joy. Therefore, no sorrow or negative feeling comes when remembering the lover.

ai.literal: Those who think - seeming - they do not think - I wonder - sneeze - that which swells - seeming - perishes.
ai.translation: My sneeze seems to build up, but then it fades away. I wonder, does he seem to think of me, but then not think of me at all?
ai.modern: தும்மல் வருவது போலத் தோன்றி வராமல் அடங்கிவிடுகிறது. அதுபோலவே அவரும் என்னை நினைப்பவர் போலத் தோன்றி, உண்மையில் நினைக்காமல் விட்டுவிட்டாரோ?
ai.explanation: This couplet plays on the traditional Tamil belief that a sneeze indicates a loved one is thinking of you. The heroine feels a sneeze building up, but it suddenly subsides ('கெடும்') without happening. She draws a direct parallel between this physical sensation and her lover's thoughts. She wonders if he started to think of her ('நினைப்பவர் போன்று') but then stopped or decided not to ('நினையார்கொல்'). The word 'சினைப்பது' (swelling or forming) perfectly captures the sensation of a sneeze that builds up but fails to release.

ai.literal: I too - am I (there) I wonder - in his heart? In my heart - oh! - is indeed - he.
ai.translation: I wonder if I am still there in his heart? Oh, he is always here in mine!
ai.modern: அவர் நெஞ்சத்தில் நாமும் இருக்கிறோமா? என் நெஞ்சத்திலோ அவர் எப்போதும் இருக்கிறாரே!
ai.explanation: The speaker, pining for her absent lover, wonders if he thinks of her as much as she thinks of him. She asks if she still exists in his heart ('அவர்நெஞ்சத்து யாமும் உளேங்கொல்'). The exclamation 'ஓஒ' (oh!) expresses her deep sigh of longing and realization. She contrasts his possible forgetfulness with her own constant devotion, noting that he is always present in her heart ('எந்நெஞ்சத்து உளரே அவர்').

ai.translation: He has locked me up securely in his own heart. Is he not ashamed to come unceasingly into mine?
ai.modern: தம்முடைய நெஞ்சத்தில் என்னை வெளியேறாமல் காவல் கொண்ட அவர், என்னுடைய நெஞ்சத்தில் மட்டும் இடைவிடாமல் வருவதற்கு வெட்கப்பட மாட்டாரா?
ai.explanation: The speaker playfully accuses her lover of a double standard. He has locked her up in his own heart, keeping her guarded so she cannot leave. Yet, he constantly enters her heart without any restriction. She wonders if he feels no shame in doing this, highlighting her constant thoughts of him and the inescapable nature of their love.

ai.literal: Else I, how exist I, alas! With him I, experienced days, to remember, exist I.
ai.translation: How else could I stay alive, alas? I survive only by remembering the days I shared with him.
ai.modern: நான் வேறு எப்படி உயிர் வாழ்வேன்? அவருடன் நான் கூடி மகிழ்ந்த நாட்களை நினைத்துப் பார்ப்பதால்தான் நான் இன்னும் உயிரோடு இருக்கிறேன்.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses her deep sorrow and longing for her absent lover. She wonders how she could possibly remain alive while enduring the pain of separation. She reveals that her only means of survival is the constant memory of the joyful days they spent together. The word 'உள்ள' (to remember) highlights that her existence now depends entirely on reliving those past moments in her mind.

ai.literal: If forgotten, what will I become, alas? Forgetting I know not; even if remembered, the heart burns.
ai.translation: I do not know how to forget him, and even when I remember him, my heart burns. Alas, what would become of me if I were to ever forget?
ai.modern: நான் அவரை மறப்பதை அறியமாட்டேன்; நினைத்தாலும் என் உள்ளம் சுடுகின்றது. அப்படியிருக்க, ஒருவேளை நான் அவரை மறந்தால் என் நிலைமை என்ன ஆகுமோ?
ai.explanation: The heroine expresses the inescapable pain of separation from her lover. She declares that she does not know how to forget him ('மறப்பு அறியேன்'), yet even the constant act of remembering him burns her heart with sorrow ('உள்ளினும் உள்ளம் சுடும்'). She wonders in despair what would happen to her if she were to actually forget him ('மறப்பின் எவன் ஆவன்'), implying that if mere memory brings such fiery agony, forgetting would mean her utter destruction. The combined expletives 'மற்கொல்' add a tone of deep pity and helpless doubt to her lament.

ai.literal: However much / even if thought / he will not be angry; / that much / is it not / lover / doing / special favor.
ai.translation: However much I think of him, he does not grow angry. Is that not the special favor my lover grants me?
ai.modern: நான் எவ்வளவு நினைத்தாலும் அவர் என் மீது கோபப்பட மாட்டார். காதலர் எனக்குச் செய்யும் சிறப்பு அவ்வளவு பெரியது அல்லவா?
ai.explanation: The speaker marvels at her lover's patience and grace. She constantly dwells on him, and while such relentless attention might normally cause annoyance, he never grows angry with her. She sees this boundless tolerance as a profound gift. The word 'சிறப்பு' (special favor or excellence) emphasizes that she views his refusal to be angered by her endless thoughts as a unique and cherished privilege granted by him.

ai.literal: Will perish my sweet life, 'different we are not' he who said, (his) grace-absence exceedingly having thought.
ai.translation: My sweet life will perish when I think deeply about the lack of grace in him who once said, 'We are not different.'
ai.modern: நாம் வேறுபட்டவர்கள் அல்லம் என்று முன்பு கூறிய காதலரின் தற்போதைய அன்பின்மையை மிகுதியாக நினைத்து என் இனிய உயிர் அழிகின்றது.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments the current coldness of her lover, contrasting it with his past intimacy. She recalls how he used to say they were not two separate beings, but one in spirit. Thinking deeply about his present lack of compassion makes her feel that her sweet life is slipping away. The word 'அளி' means grace or tender love, and its absence is what breaks her heart.

ai.literal: Without leaving, him who went, with eyes to see, do not set, may you live, moon.
ai.translation: O moon, may you live long! Do not set, so that I may see with my own eyes him who departed without ever leaving my heart.
ai.modern: நிலவே, நீ நீடூழி வாழ்வாயாக! என் நெஞ்சை விட்டு அகலாமல் பிரிந்து சென்ற என் காதலரை நான் என் கண்களால் காணும் பொருட்டு நீ மறையாமல் இருப்பாயாக.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks directly to the moon (மதி), wishing it a long life (வாழி) as she begs it not to set (படாஅதி). She relies on the moonlight to search for her lover, who has physically journeyed away (சென்றாரை) yet remains constantly in her thoughts without leaving (விடாஅது). The poetic elongation of sounds (alapeṭai) in the words for 'without leaving' and 'do not set' beautifully mirrors her drawn-out yearning and her desire to stretch the night.
